title: State v. P.J. & Ors. (Opera House Diamond Vault Staged Burglary Case)
citation: Independent Contributor: Judicial Academy Mock Trial Case Study (Case #BLIND-2024-F05)
confidence_note: High - Customs airport seizure of stolen diamonds and electronic lock audit

ground_truth.culprit_summary: Jeweler Owner Pravin J. and Accomplices (Staged Theft)
ground_truth.rationale: Digital lock audit shows owner's authentic PIN opened vault without forced entry. Customs intercepted owner's brother-in-law boarding flight to Dubai with the missing diamonds.

hypotheses.label: Jeweler Owner Pravin J. (Staged Insurance Burglary)
hypotheses.statement: Owner staged an elaborate fake burglary using his master credentials to claim ₹12 Crore insurance while smuggling stones to Dubai via kin.

hypotheses.label: Estranged Nephew Yash J. (Duplicate Keycard Theft)
hypotheses.statement: Nephew addicted to high-stakes gambling cloned vault keycard and looted safe while uncle was away at trade exhibition.

hypotheses.label: Professional Underground Safecracking Syndicate
hypotheses.statement: Organized criminal gang tunneled through sewer conduit and utilized electromagnetic lock bypass to breach subterranean vault.

exhibits.name: Godrej Electronic Time-Lock & Master Vault Audit Telemetry
exhibits.text: Digital diagnostic read-out from the vault controller demonstrates the door was opened at 23:42 IST with owner Pravin J.'s authentic Master PIN and mechanical key. Zero acoustic sensor alarms, drill torque triggers, or electronic tampering events were logged during the incident.

exhibits.name: Forensic Structural Examination of Vault Walls & Basement
exhibits.text: Physical inspection of masonry and subterranean drainage conduits confirms reinforced concrete walls are completely intact with no drilling, tunnel breaches, or structural compromises.

exhibits.name: Mumbai Customs Intelligence Air Cargo Seizure Dossier
exhibits.text: Air Intelligence Unit at Terminal 2 intercepted Pravin J.'s brother-in-law Nilesh boarding Emirates flight EK-501 to Dubai. 4,200 carats of certified cut diamonds matching the serial numbers on the victim's vault ledger were recovered concealed in false bottoms of hard-shell luggage.

exhibits.name: Bank Consortium SARFAESI Default & Debt Ledger
exhibits.text: Certified forensic financial audit showing jeweler's enterprise had defaulted on ₹18 Crore working capital facilities with loan recall notices issued 10 days before the alleged heist.

adversarial_exhibit.name: Planted Goa Casino Debt Ledger Scribble
adversarial_exhibit.text: Photocopied handwritten IOU slip claiming nephew Yash owed ₹5 Crore to Goa bookies.
